findings.title: setIgnoreMouseEvents(..., {forward:true}) keeps a system-wide low-level mouse hook in the main process 24/7, for nothing
findings.evidence: main.js:199 and :797 put the overlay in setIgnoreMouseEvents(true, { forward: true }), which is its permanent state. On Windows, Electron implements `forward` with SetWindowsHookEx(WH_MOUSE_LL) on the browser main thread (native_window_views_win.cc, SetForwardMouseMessages/MouseHookProc). It also PostMessage()s a WM_MOUSEMOVE to the overlay for every system mouse move inside its client rect, which here is the whole screen. Windows runs LL hooks synchronously on the hooking thread before delivering input. Since 2637de3, hover detection uses the 16 ms getCursorScreenPoint poll (:757-789). overlay.js's mousemove handler returns unless inCapture (overlay.js:84-85), and in capture mode ignore=false, so forwarding is already off. Forwarding is a leftover.
findings.behavior_change: none. Click-through is the same: both variants set WS_EX_TRANSPARENT, and hover/drag rely on the poll plus real events in capture mode. Side effect: Chromium now receives WM_MOUSELEAVE when capture ends (forward mode swallowed it), so CSS :hover clears properly.
findings.risk: Low. Relies on how Electron implements `forward` on Windows (high confidence; unchanged for many majors).
findings.value: Removes a global hook that runs on every mouse event on a gaming PC (1000-8000 Hz mice) all day. Each event wakes MemeDrop's main thread and posts a WM_MOUSEMOVE into the overlay pipeline. Game mouse latency no longer depends on main-thread stalls (sync config writes, GC, IPC bursts). Biggest idle win in this area.

findings.title: Electron 33 (Chromium 130) is end-of-life while the overlay auto-renders attacker-supplied media
findings.evidence: package.json:21 has "electron": "^33.4.11" (lock 33.4.11), and the caret stays on 33.x. Electron supports only the 3 latest majors; 33 lost support when 36 shipped (spring 2025). In Nov 2026 the overlay therefore runs a Chromium about 18 months behind on security fixes. Its renderer decodes attacker-chosen media with zero interaction. Any member of a guild where a friend ran /link can /drop any file labelled image/video/audio (the bot only checks Discord's contentType, bot/index.js:541-548), and overlay.js puts media.url straight into /
findings.proposed_change:
- Bump `electron` to the current stable major (supported majors in Nov 2026 are roughly 43-45; check electronjs.org/docs/latest/tutorial/electron-timelines) and regenerate package-lock.json.
- Bump electron-builder (24 -> current) and electron-updater in the same PR.
- Keep it current afterwards: Dependabot/Renovate on overlay/, or a CI step that fails on an EOL major.
- Read the breaking-change notes for the APIs used here: transparent + focusable:false windows, setIgnoreMouseEvents, setAlwaysOnTop('screen-saver'), Tray/Menu, globalShortcut, setLoginItemSettings, contextBridge/ipcMain.handle.
- Smoke-test on Windows: click-through + drag, tray, --hidden autostart, auto-update from 1.5.1.
Cannot be built in this sandbox (registry unreachable).
findings.behavior_change: none intended
findings.risk: Medium: a multi-major jump can change window/tray behaviour on Windows; needs manual QA before release.
findings.value: Closes the product's largest attack surface: a zero-click parser of remote content running 24/7 on every friend's PC. A compromised renderer can also call every privileged IPC (see ipc-privileged-unrestricted).

findings.title: Each store.get() re-reads and re-parses config.json and each set() rewrites it with fsync, synchronously, ~12 reads + 1 write per drop
findings.evidence: conf 10.2 (the backend of electron-store 8.2) keeps nothing in memory. get(k) runs the `store` getter, which is fs.readFileSync + JSON.parse of the whole file. set() re-reads it, then calls atomically.writeFileSync (temp file, write, fsync, rename); on Windows EPERM/EBUSY it busy-retries synchronously, then throws. Per drop (:489-491): recordHistory does a get+set (:117-118), isMuted 2 gets (:73,:83), currentDropSettings 8 gets (:337-344). That is ~12 parses of a file that holds the 20-entry history, plus 1 fsync'd write, all before the 'drop' IPC is sent. While idle, :853 and the settings window's 30 s poll (->:684) keep re-reading it forever. settings:set writes once per key (:629). An fs error thrown in the ws handler is uncaught and shows a main-process error dialog.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: a transient fs error (AV lock on rename, disk full) no longer pops Electron's main-process error dialog or loses the drop. Otherwise none, except that hand-edits of config.json while the app runs are no longer picked up (conf's watch option isn't used anyway).
findings.cross_component: none (prerequisite for electron-store-dependency-weight; the settings:set whitelist can use setMany)
findings.risk: Low. High confidence that conf <= 10 has no in-memory cache (it re-reads to support multiple processes).
findings.value: Removes ~12 synchronous readFileSync+JSON.parse calls and one fsync'd rename from each drop's critical path. That runs on the thread that also serves IPC and, today, the mouse hook. No disk reads at idle instead of 2-3 every 30 s forever, and one write per settings change instead of one per key.

findings.title: WebSocket opening handshake has no timeout: the overlay can stay on 'connexion…' forever
findings.evidence: main.js:414 calls `new WebSocket(url)` without options. The 75 s heartbeat is armed only in 'open' (:420) and on messages (:430). ws 8 only sets a request timeout when `handshakeTimeout` is given (default undefined). Suppose TCP/TLS gets through but the 101 response never comes, for example a proxy holding the request, a captive portal, or a Wi-Fi switch or sleep during the handshake leaving a half-open socket with nothing outstanding on our side. Then neither 'open', 'error' nor 'close' fires and scheduleReconnect() is never called. The UI stays on 'connexion…' and drops are lost until the user clicks Reconnect or restarts. maxPayload also defaults to 100 MiB.
findings.proposed_change:
`try { sock = new WebSocket(url, { handshakeTimeout: 20_000, maxPayload: 1024 * 1024 }); }`
On timeout, ws aborts the request and emits 'error' then 'close', so the existing close handler reconnects with backoff. Bot messages are a few KB; 1 MiB caps what a bogus server can make the main process buffer (default 100 MiB).
Optional, same area (:509-514), small value at a handful of clients:
- add jitter: `const base = Math.min(30_000, 1000 * 1.6 ** Math.min(reconnectAttempts, 8)); reconnectTimer = setTimeout(connectWS, base * (0.75 + Math.random() * 0.5));`
- reset reconnectAttempts on the first message instead of on 'open'. Today a server that accepts and then closes immediately is retried every 1.6 s.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: a stalled handshake recovers by itself within ~20 s
findings.risk: Low; both options exist in ws 8. 20 s is ample for a Fly.io cold start (the bot's HTTP server listens before the Discord login).
findings.value: The connection now repairs itself in a 24/7 app: no more silent 'connexion…' hangs after a Wi-Fi change or a sleep during a connect.

findings.title: settings:set and the other privileged IPC accept any key/value from any renderer, including the overlay
findings.evidence: settings:set (:624-629) saves every key it receives, `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(patch)) store.set(k, v);`, including linkIdentity (token), dropHistory and muteUntil, with no type check. Both windows load the same preload (:189, :243) and no handler checks event.sender, yet the overlay renderer is the one parsing untrusted media. A compromised overlay renderer can call setSettings({serverUrl:'wss://evil'}). That triggers connectWS() (:639), and on open main sends {type:'register', identity} with the HMAC re-link token (:425-426) to the attacker, who can then register as the victim on the real bot. Bad types are also saved: {dropHistory:5} makes recordHistory throw inside the ws handler. open-external (:753) opens any http(s) URL from any window, and drop:react(null) throws in main.
findings.proposed_change:
Sender guard + whitelist:
```js
const isFrom = (w, e) => !!w && !w.isDestroyed() && e.sender.id === w.webContents.id;
const num = (lo, hi) => (v) => typeof v === 'number' && v >= lo && v <= hi;   // NaN échoue
const bool = (v) => typeof v === 'boolean', hhmm = (v) => /^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$/.test(v);
const RULES = {
  serverUrl: (v) => typeof v === 'string' && v.length <= 2048 && /^wss?:\/\/\S+$/i.test(v),
  volume: num(0, 1), musicVolume: num(0, 1), opacity: num(0.2, 1), duration: num(1, 30), videoDuration: num(1, 30),
  soundOnArrival: bool, spotlightOnDrop: bool, autostart: bool, paused: bool,
  overlayDisplayId: (v) => v === null || Number.isFinite(v),
  theme: (v) => ['classic', 'neon', 'fire', 'mono'].includes(v),
  avoidZone: (v) => ['none', 'center', 'top', 'bottom'].includes(v),
  quietHours: (v) => !!v && bool(v.enabled) && hhmm(v.start) && hhmm(v.end),
};
```
- settings:set: `if (!isFrom(settingsWin, e) || !raw || typeof raw !== 'object') return false;`, then keep only keys passing RULES (copy quietHours as {enabled, start, end}) and run the rest of the handler on that patch.
- isFrom(settingsWin) guard on connection:*, mute:set (accept null/0/-1/1..1440), history:clear/replay, update:*, test-drop and open-external.
- isFrom(overlayWin) guard on drop:react (destructure `arg || {}`), stage-empty and overlay:*.
- open-external: `try { const u = new URL(String(url)); if (u.protocol === 'https:' && u.hostname === 'github.com') shell.openExternal(u.href); } catch {}`.
findings.behavior_change: none for the shipped UI (settings.js only sends these keys with these types; overlay.js only reads settings:get and uses overlay channels)
findings.cross_component: none; optional: give the overlay window a reduced preload
findings.risk: Low. Keep the read-only handlers (settings:get, connection:get, history:get...) open to both windows: overlay.js:916 reads the theme.
findings.value: Closes the token-theft and config-corruption paths from the window that parses untrusted content. Malformed IPC can no longer turn into main-process exceptions.

findings.title: No will-navigate / window-open / permission handlers: a drag-and-drop hijacks or breaks the settings window
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: dropping files or links on a MemeDrop window no longer replaces its page; middle-clicking the 'comment ça marche' link no longer opens a stray window
findings.risk: Low; verify that the copy-code button still works.
findings.value: Closes the classic Electron navigation, new-window and permission holes (items on Electron's security checklist) and a real UX trap. This matters more because the renderers run an EOL Chromium.

findings.title: Overlay renderer crash/reload is not handled: drops silently lost, cursor poll and guard leak
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: the overlay recovers by itself after a renderer crash
findings.risk: Low (the reload loop is capped at 3 per minute).
findings.value: A 24/7 app can no longer get stuck for good in a silent 'drops invisible' state with a 60 Hz timer still running.

findings.title: The full-screen topmost overlay window stays shown 24/7, even with nothing to display (unverified gaming impact)
findings.evidence: createOverlayWindow shows the overlay on 'ready-to-show' (:206) and nothing ever hides it except the tray toggle (:287-291). So a screen-sized always-on-top ('screen-saver') layered window always covers whatever game runs on that display, although it is empty more than 99% of the time. On Windows, a visible window over a flip-model fullscreen/borderless game normally makes DWM compose the game instead of using independent flip / direct scan-out. That adds latency and can interfere with VRR; GPUs with multi-plane overlay (MPO) support may reduce the effect. Not measured here: compare PresentMon's PresentMode column with the overlay hidden via the tray versus shown.
findings.behavior_change: none visible if it works (the idle window is fully transparent); must check that showing it causes no flash and no focus change
findings.cross_component: none (reuses the existing 'stage-empty' message; same media-less tracking as top-guard-leak-and-noop)
findings.risk: Medium. Showing and hiding a transparent topmost window over games needs QA: showInactive only, first-drop latency, tray semantics. The benefit is unverified, so measure with PresentMon first.
findings.value: If confirmed, removes the overlay's main in-game cost while idle, the DWM composition of the game, which is what friends actually feel. While idle there is also nothing left to composite or hit-test.

findings.title: Top guard leaks after rain/TTS-only drops and practically never acts
findings.evidence: showDropOnOverlay starts the 2 s guard for every drop (:351). The only stop is 'stage-empty' (:752), which overlay.js notifyIfIdle() sends only from releaseSlot(), i.e. only for drops that took a slot. Rain-only and TTS-only drops, and their history replays, return early in renderDrop (overlay.js:561-566) without touching `active`. The interval (:154-160) then runs until a later media drop ends, possibly forever. Its body also only acts if !isAlwaysOnTop(), which stays true after setAlwaysOnTop(true) (:197) unless another process clears WS_EX_TOPMOST. Being covered by another topmost window doesn't change it, so the guard never brings the overlay back on top; the per-drop enforceTop() -> moveTop() does. The same goes for the 'blur' handler (:201-203) on a focusable:false window.
findings.proposed_change:
Minimal fix: in showDropOnOverlay, `if (payload.media) startTopGuard();` (rain/TTS drops keep the one-shot enforceTop()).
Simpler and equivalent in practice:
- delete topGuardTimer/startTopGuard/stopTopGuard and the 'blur' handler;
- delete the isAlwaysOnTop() branch of enforceTop(), keeping `overlayWin.moveTop()` (setAlwaysOnTop is applied once at :197);
- keep 'stage-empty' as a no-op, or use it for overlay-shown-while-idle.
If a periodic bring-to-top is really wanted, make it work instead: interval body `overlayWin.moveTop()`, started only for media drops.
Related (overlay.js, shared with Android): playAudioDrop (:490-544) has no load timeout, unlike videos (15 s), so a stalled audio URL holds its slot and also blocks 'stage-empty'.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: no 2 s main-process wakeup left running after rain/TTS drops; otherwise none
findings.risk: Low.
findings.value: Stops a timer leak in a 24/7 process and removes ~20 lines that don't do what their comment says.

findings.title: Ctrl+Alt+S / Ctrl+Alt+M are registered as global hotkeys in production
findings.evidence: whenReady (:841-850) registers globalShortcut 'Control+Alt+S' and 'Control+Alt+M' for the whole lifetime of the packaged app (autostart, 24/7). Global hotkeys are taken system-wide: while MemeDrop runs, other apps never receive them. Examples: JetBrains IDEs (Ctrl+Alt+S Settings, Ctrl+Alt+M Extract Method), and AltGr combos, since AltGr is Ctrl+Alt on Windows (AltGr+S types ś on Polish layouts). They are also redundant: the tray already opens the overlay DevTools (:298-303), and in the settings window Electron's default menu gives Ctrl+Shift+I (autoHideMenuBar only hides the bar).
findings.proposed_change: Wrap both registrations (:841-850) in `if (!app.isPackaged) { ... }`, or delete them. Nothing else is needed: the tray opens the overlay DevTools, and Ctrl+Shift+I (default application menu) opens the settings DevTools.
findings.behavior_change: visible (bugfix): packaged builds stop taking over Ctrl+Alt+S / Ctrl+Alt+M; DevTools stay reachable through the tray (overlay) and Ctrl+Shift+I (settings)
findings.risk: Very low.
findings.value: MemeDrop no longer steals these shortcuts on friends' PCs.

findings.title: Autostart registers the wrong executable for the portable build and in dev
findings.evidence:
:633 and :823-827 call setLoginItemSettings({ openAtLogin, openAsHidden, args:['--hidden'] }) without `path`, so the Run entry uses process.execPath.
- Portable target (package.json:49-56): execPath is the copy the portable launcher extracts to %TEMP% and deletes on exit, so autostart (on by default) never works for portable users. electron-builder exposes the real exe in PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_FILE.
- `npm start`: execPath is node_modules\electron\dist\electron.exe without the app path, so the next login opens the bare Electron default app. Electron's default Run value name comes from the AppUserModelId, which :812 also sets to 'com.memedrop.overlay' in dev, so a dev run likely overwrites the installed app's entry.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: autostart works for portable users, and dev runs no longer overwrite the installed app's autostart
findings.risk: Low; check the HKCU Run value after enabling autostart in the portable exe.
findings.value: Autostart, which is on by default, now works for every build flavour.

findings.title: A corrupted config.json crashes the app at every launch
findings.evidence: new Store({ defaults }) (:22) runs at module load without clearInvalidConfig, and conf 10 defaults it to false. If config.json is not valid JSON, the constructor throws. Causes include a power loss during the non-atomic EXDEV fallback write conf uses on some Windows setups, a disk error, or a hand edit. The result is Electron's 'A JavaScript error occurred in the main process' box at every launch, including autostart, with no tray and no overlay, until the user finds and deletes userData\config.json.
findings.proposed_change: Add `clearInvalidConfig: true` to the Store options: settings reset to defaults and the user re-links once, instead of a dead app. Optional, before constructing: try JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(app.getPath('userData'), 'config.json'), 'utf8')), and on SyntaxError rename the file to config.corrupt-<ts>.json so it can be inspected.
findings.behavior_change: bugfix: corrupted settings fall back to defaults instead of a crash at startup
findings.cross_component: none (also covered by store-disk-io-per-access / electron-store-dependency-weight snippets)
findings.risk: Very low.
findings.value: Turns a crash loop that a non-technical friend cannot fix into a one-time re-link.

findings.title: Server drop payloads are forwarded and saved without scheme or size checks
findings.evidence: The 'drop' message is forwarded as-is ({ ...payload, settings }, :352) and its strings are copied into dropHistory (:99-116), which is saved in config.json; electron-store re-reads that file on every get(). A bogus or compromised server, or a man-in-the-middle (serverUrl also accepts ws://), can make the file:// overlay page load file:// or LAN http URLs as media. It can also push multi-MB caption/tts/url strings into the history file (ws maxPayload defaults to 100 MiB), slowing every later store access.
findings.proposed_change:
- In the 'drop' case, before recordHistory/showDropOnOverlay: `const okUrl = (u) => u == null || (typeof u === 'string' && u.length <= 2048 && /^https?:\/\//i.test(u));`, and ignore the message unless okUrl(msg.media?.url) && okUrl(msg.music?.url) && okUrl(msg.ttsUrl) && okUrl(msg.from?.avatar).
- In recordHistory, cap fields the way the bot does (bot/index.js:589-624): caption <= 80 chars, tts <= 200, from <= 64, rain <= 5 items.
- Plus maxPayload from ws-handshake-no-timeout.
findings.behavior_change: none with the real bot (it only sends https Discord/bot URLs and bounded fields)
findings.risk: Low; keep http allowed for a self-hosted bot on localhost.
findings.value: Limits what a misbehaving server can make the overlay fetch or the config file store.

findings.title: Hidden settings window keeps a full renderer alive forever; the global anti-throttling switches only serve it
findings.proposed_change:
(a) Delete the two appendSwitch lines; the overlay is unaffected thanks to backgroundThrottling:false.
(b) Bigger win: let the settings window really close. Remove the 'close' -> hide handler (:251-256) and add `settingsWin.on('closed', () => { settingsWin = null; });`. createSettingsWindow() already recreates the window on demand (tray click, second instance). settings.js init() fetches everything again: settings, connection, history and update state; the tab and badge come from localStorage. For (b), flush the 150 ms debounce on close in settings.js: `window.addEventListener('beforeunload', () => { if (_flushTimer) { clearTimeout(_flushTimer); window.memedrop.setSettings({ ..._pending }); } });`.
findings.behavior_change: (b) visible: reopening the settings is a cold page load (a few hundred ms) instead of an instant show
findings.risk: Low.
findings.value: Frees a renderer process (usually tens of MB) and its timers in a tray app that runs for weeks. (a) alone lets Chromium put the hidden page in the background.

findings.title: Settings-only broadcasts are also sent to the overlay renderer (full history on every drop)
findings.evidence: Four copies of the same loop send to BrowserWindow.getAllWindows(): history-update (:119-121, :690-692), connection-state (:393-395) and update-state (:533-535). overlay.js listens to none of them (only onDrop, onSettingsUpdate, onCursor). So each drop also serializes the full 20-entry history (long Discord URLs) to the overlay. That message is queued just before the 'drop' message itself, since recordHistory runs first. The overlay also gets every connection change and every download-progress tick.
findings.behavior_change: none
findings.risk: Very low.
findings.value: Less IPC and deserialization work in the overlay renderer exactly when a drop arrives, and simpler code.

findings.title: Cursor poll keeps sending while the overlay captures the mouse and calls getBounds() every tick
findings.evidence: The 16 ms poll (:770-779) runs while a visual drop is on screen. Whenever the mouse moves, it calls overlayWin.getBounds() and sends 'overlay:cursor'. During hover/drag the overlay is in capture mode and the renderer throws these messages away (overlay.js:77 `if (inCapture) return;`), so up to 62.5 useless IPC/s. getBounds() is a native call even though the window is movable:false and only moves through repositionOverlay(). The cost is modest (only while drops are shown).
findings.proposed_change:
- Add `let overlayCapturing = false, overlayBounds = null;`.
- In 'overlay:set-ignore-mouse': `overlayCapturing = !ignore; if (ignore) _lastCursor = null;` (forces a resend when capture ends).
- In the poll: `if (overlayCapturing) return;` before getCursorScreenPoint, and `const b = overlayBounds || (overlayBounds = overlayWin.getBounds());`.
- Reset `overlayBounds = null` in repositionOverlay() and createOverlayWindow(), and reset overlayCapturing in the crash/reload handler.
findings.behavior_change: none
findings.risk: Very low.
findings.value: Small: removes useless IPC and native calls while a drop is hovered or dragged.

findings.title: paintWhenInitiallyHidden sits in webPreferences, where it is ignored, and would break the overlay if moved; plus unused IPC
findings.evidence: :193 puts `paintWhenInitiallyHidden: false` inside webPreferences, but it is a top-level BrowserWindow option (documented next to `show`). Today it does nothing, which matches the overlay showing fine. Moving it to its documented place would break the app: Electron documents that false stops 'ready-to-show' from firing, and :206 is the only place the overlay is shown. Also unused: ipcMain 'mute:get' (:683) and preload getMute (preload.js:25) have no caller in settings.js, overlay.js or the Android assets.
findings.proposed_change: Delete line 193. Optionally delete `ipcMain.handle('mute:get', ...)` and `getMute` in preload.js to shrink the exposed API.
findings.behavior_change: none
findings.risk: None.
findings.value: Removes a misleading option that would hide the overlay for good if someone 'fixed' it.

findings.title: DEFAULT_SERVER is read on the user's PC at runtime; the documented build-time override does nothing
findings.evidence: :8-9 `process.env.DEFAULT_SERVER || 'wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev'` runs inside the packaged app, and electron-builder doesn't inline env vars. Yet README.md:91 ('main.js already reads from a build-time env var'), RELEASE.md:40 and windows.yml (DEFAULT_SERVER on the build step) all set it at build time, where it has no effect: the hard-coded fallback is what ships. The other way round, a DEFAULT_SERVER variable in a user's environment silently changes a fresh install's server.
findings.proposed_change:
Option 1, dev-only: `const DEFAULT_SERVER = (!app.isPackaged && process.env.DEFAULT_SERVER) || 'wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev';`, and fix README/RELEASE/windows.yml.
Option 2, a real build-time value: build with `-c.extraMetadata.defaultServer=$DEFAULT_SERVER` and read `require('./package.json').defaultServer || 'wss://memedrop-bot.fly.dev'`.
findings.behavior_change: none for current releases
findings.risk: Very low.
findings.value: Removes a misleading way to configure the default server; the next server move would otherwise silently keep the old default.

findings.title: electron-store brings 28 of the 45 production packages (two copies of ajv 8) for one JSON file
findings.evidence: The package-lock dependency closure of electron-store 8.2.0 is 28 packages, none shared with electron-updater or ws, out of 45 production packages. It includes conf 10.2.0, ajv 8.20.0 twice (conf/node_modules/ajv and ajv-formats/node_modules/ajv), ajv-formats, fast-uri, json-schema-traverse x2, atomically, dot-prop, pkg-up/find-up/locate-path/p-*, semver and type-fest. conf loads ajv/ajv-formats at module load although main.js uses no schema, so every launch (autostart at login) loads that code for nothing.
findings.behavior_change: none (also covers the corrupted-config fix)
findings.risk: Low to medium: test the new persistence code on a fresh install, an upgrade with an existing config, a corrupted file, and a rename blocked by antivirus on Windows (the catch keeps the in-memory state).
findings.value: Smaller asar, faster cold start at login and fewer modules loaded in the 24/7 main process; one less dependency tree to patch.

findings.title: All ~55 Chromium locale packs are shipped; only fr/en are useful
findings.evidence: The build config (package.json:24-68) has no electronLanguages, so electron-builder ships every Electron locales/*.pak (tens of MB unpacked). They only translate Chromium-internal strings; MemeDrop's own UI is French HTML. The portable target (:49-56) also re-extracts the whole app to %TEMP% at every launch.
findings.proposed_change: Add `"electronLanguages": ["en-US", "fr"]` to "build". electron-builder then deletes the other locales/*.pak after packing; en-US must stay as Chromium's fallback. Check dist/win-unpacked/locales after the CI build.
findings.behavior_change: Chromium-internal strings (form validation bubbles, media error text) fall back to English on systems whose language is neither French nor English
findings.risk: Low.
findings.value: Smaller installer and install footprint, and less to extract at every portable launch.
